intro: Manchester rewards visitors with world-class museums, a legendary music scene and a buzzing food and bar culture. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metrolink tram is quick and covers the centre and suburbs; Zone 1 is free with some train tickets.
Bee Network buses are yellow and franchised; single fares are around £2.
Taxis are metered; Uber, Bolt and local apps all work in the city.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is costly; use park and ride instead.
The centre is compact and walkable; Starling Bikes offers bike share with e-bikes.
No ferry in the city; the nearest cruise terminal is Liverpool.

old_trafford.name: Old Trafford
old_trafford.price_text: Stadium tour prices vary; check on the day
old_trafford.hours: Tour times vary by match calendar; check on the day
old_trafford.tip: Book a stadium tour online in advance and avoid home match days if you want a quiet visit.

science_industry_museum.name: Science and Industry Museum
science_industry_museum.price_text: Free entry; some special exhibitions charge
science_industry_museum.hours: Daily roughly 10:00–17:00; check on the day
science_industry_museum.tip: Start with the Power Hall and textile machinery to understand why Manchester grew.

manchester_art_gallery.name: Manchester Art Gallery
manchester_art_gallery.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–17:00; closed Monday, check on the day
manchester_art_gallery.tip: The Pre-Raphaelite rooms are the highlight; allow an hour and a half.

chethams_library.name: Chetham's Library
chethams_library.price_text: Small fee or donation; check on the day
chethams_library.hours: Weekdays only, limited hours; check on the day
chethams_library.tip: This is the oldest free public library in the English-speaking world; book a short tour slot.

etihad_stadium.name: Etihad Stadium
etihad_stadium.price_text: Stadium tour prices vary; check on the day
etihad_stadium.hours: Tour times vary by match calendar; check on the day
etihad_stadium.tip: The stadium is a short tram ride east of the centre; combine it with a walk in nearby Ancoats.

university_of_manchester.name: University of Manchester
university_of_manchester.tip: Walk Oxford Road past the main quad and the Whitworth is a short bus ride further on.

afflecks.name: Afflecks
afflecks.hours: Daily roughly 10:00–18:00; check on the day
afflecks.tip: Four floors of independent stalls in the Northern Quarter; good for quirky gifts.

northern_quarter_walk.name: Northern Quarter street-art walk
northern_quarter_walk.price_text: Free self-guided; paid tours from about GBP 12
northern_quarter_walk.tip: Wander the side streets around Thomas Street and Oldham Street for murals and record shops.

mackie_mayor.name: Mackie Mayor food hall
mackie_mayor.hours: Daily, lunch to late evening; check on the day
mackie_mayor.tip: Busy at weekends; go early for a seat at the communal tables.

john_rylands.name: John Rylands Library
john_rylands.hours: Tue–Sat roughly 10:00–17:00; check on the day
john_rylands.tip: The neo-Gothic reading room looks like a cathedral; go for opening time to avoid crowds.

castlefield_urban_heritage.name: Castlefield Urban Heritage Park
castlefield_urban_heritage.tip: Walk the canal towpaths past the Roman fort remains and old brick warehouses.

canal_street.name: Canal Street
canal_street.price_text: Free to walk; bars charge for drinks
canal_street.tip: The heart of the Gay Village; liveliest on weekend evenings.

piccadilly_market.name: Piccadilly Gardens and market area
piccadilly_market.tip: A central meeting point and tram hub; use it as a start for a walk down Market Street.

ancoats_canals.name: Ancoats canal walk
ancoats_canals.tip: Old cotton mills turned into flats and cafes; walk the Ashton Canal towards the Etihad.

cutting_room_square.name: Cutting Room Square
cutting_room_square.hours: Venues vary; check on the day
cutting_room_square.tip: A small square of independent food and drink spots in Ancoats; good for a relaxed lunch.

st_anns_square.name: St Ann's Square
st_anns_square.tip: Quiet square with the Royal Exchange theatre nearby; a good pause between shopping streets.

royal_exchange.name: Royal Exchange Theatre
royal_exchange.hours: Box office and bar daytime; shows evenings
royal_exchange.tip: The theatre-in-the-round sits inside a grand old cotton exchange; check what is on.

manchester_cathedral.name: Manchester Cathedral
manchester_cathedral.hours: Daily roughly 08:30–17:00; check on the day
manchester_cathedral.tip: Step inside for the carved choir stalls, then walk to Chetham's next door.

whitworth.name: The Whitworth
whitworth.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–17:00; check on the day
whitworth.tip: Art gallery and park in one; the cafe looks over the park.

curry_mile.name: Curry Mile, Rusholme
curry_mile.tip: A long strip of South Asian restaurants; take the bus down Oxford Road.

stays.why: Next to the main train station and tram stops; easiest base for a short first visit.
Independent bars, cafés and record shops on your doorstep; walkable to the centre.
Central and close to the canal, museums and big shopping streets.
Quiet former mill district with good food and drink; about 15 minutes' walk to Piccadilly.

food: Try a proper Northern Sunday roast or a pie in a traditional pub; prices vary, so check the menu.
Curry Mile on Wilmslow Road is the classic spot for South Asian food; many places are cheap and casual.
The Northern Quarter has the densest cluster of independent cafés and brunch spots.
Look for food halls and markets for a mix of stalls at mid-range prices; check opening days on the day.
Book popular restaurants ahead for Friday and Saturday nights, especially in Ancoats and the Northern Quarter.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a tram or train trip out to a nearby town or the countryside; check times on the day.
Football fans can add a stadium tour; book ahead as slots sell out.
Add a live music night at a smaller venue instead of a second museum.
